title: Sales Process Consulting for Owners | Vestis Solutions
description: Sales process consulting for owner-led businesses: faster replies, real follow-up, clear quotes, better closing, and help hiring your first salesperson.
h1: Sales process consulting that turns more of your leads into jobs
intro: The phone rings while you're on a job, and by the time you call back they've hired someone else. Quotes go out and nobody follows up. You're paying to get leads, then losing them somewhere between the first call and the signed contract.
definition: Sales process consulting is outside help to map and fix how your business handles a lead from first contact to signed job: how fast you reply, how you follow up, how quotes are built and presented, how deals are closed, and who owns each step.

paras: Most owner-led businesses don't need more leads first. They need to stop losing the ones they have. The leaks tend to show up in the same places.
bullets: Slow replies: calls and form fills that wait hours or days for a response
No follow-up: one quote sent, then silence
Unclear quotes: confusing scope or price, with no next step for the customer
No owner: everyone assumes someone else called them back
No numbers: nobody tracks leads, quotes sent or close rate

sections.h2: How sales process consulting works with me
paras: I start with a sales process review. I walk through how your leads are handled today, from first call to signed job, with you and whoever answers the phone. We look at real leads from the last few months and follow each one to see where it went.

Then we fix it with your team, one leak at a time. That might mean a reply standard and a missed-call text back, a follow-up sequence in the CRM you already use, a cleaner quote template with a clear next step, or a simple script for the first call. Each step gets an owner and a number, so you can see whether it's working.
Lead handling is usually first because it's the cheapest win. A lead you already paid for, answered fast and followed up properly, is worth more than a new one.

Many owners are the only salesperson, and it caps growth. When it's time to hire, I help you define the seat, write the job description, set pay and targets you can afford, and plan the first 90 days. This often comes up in our owner sessions.

A new salesperson needs a process to step into. If the steps, scripts and follow-up are written down first, they ramp faster and you aren't the one training them on every call. Compensation agreements and contracts should still be reviewed by your CPA or attorney.

faq.q: What does a sales process consultant do?
faq.a: A sales process consultant maps how your leads move from first contact to signed job, finds where they're lost, and fixes those steps with your team. That covers reply speed, follow-up, quotes, closing and who owns each step. The goal is more jobs from the leads you already get.

faq.q: How fast should I respond to a new lead?
faq.a: As fast as you can, ideally within minutes during business hours. Homeowners and property managers often contact several companies, and the first to respond has a real advantage. A missed-call text back and a clear owner for incoming leads make fast replies possible even when everyone is on a job.

faq.q: How many times should I follow up on a quote?
faq.a: More than once, and on a set schedule. Many quotes are lost simply because nobody followed up. A simple sequence of a call, a text and an email over one to two weeks, set up in your CRM, keeps the job alive without relying on memory.

faq.q: When should a small business hire its first salesperson?
faq.a: Usually when the owner's time selling is the main thing limiting growth and there's enough lead flow to keep someone busy. Before hiring, write down the sales process, define the role and set targets. A salesperson with a clear process ramps faster than one who has to invent it.

faq.q: How do I improve my close rate?
faq.a: Reply faster, follow up on every quote, and make your proposals clear about scope, price and the next step. Track leads, quotes sent and jobs won each week so you can see which change helped. Small fixes in each step usually add up more than one big change.

faq.q: Do you work with contractors outside Charlotte?
faq.a: Yes. I'm based in Charlotte, NC and work with owner-led businesses across the US. The sales process review and the fixes happen over video calls and screen shares, with short check-ins with your team. That includes whoever answers your phones, since they're often the first step in the sale.
